settings.2fa.title: Two-factor authentication
settings.2fa.explained: Two-factor authentication provides an additional layer of security for your account by adding an additional authentication step during login. This prevents malicious actors from gaining access to your account if your first login step is compromised.
settings.2fa.otpExplained: Two-factor authentication with OTP code creates one-time password via authenticator applications (like Authy, Google/Microsoft Authenticator, etc.) that you enter on login.
settings.2fa.confirmCode: Code that shows in your authentication application
settings.2fa.codeHeading: If you can't scan QR code, you can manually enter the following code:
settings.2fa.instructions1: Install and open authenticator application of your choice (Authy, Google/Microsoft Authenticator, FreeOTP, etc.)
settings.2fa.instructions2: Select "Add account" (can be a visible "+" icon or can be hidden in a menu)
settings.2fa.instructions3: Scan the QR code presented on the screen here or if not possible enter the code bellow.
settings.2fa.instructions4: Type in the 6 numbers that appear on the screen into the input here to finish.

settings.integrations.intro: Connect Literary Universe to services you already use. Each connection belongs to one of your blogs, universes, organizations or groups.
settings.integrations.luma.description: Your public events appear on a Luma calendar and stay up to date as you edit them here. People who register on Luma with the email address of their Literary Universe account are marked as attending. Luma's API needs a Luma Plus calendar. <link>Create an API key</link> for the calendar and paste it below.

settings.integrations.basecamp.summary: Post new blog posts, chapters and events to a Basecamp project's Campfire.
settings.integrations.basecamp.intro: Post a line to a Basecamp project's Campfire whenever something here is published. In Basecamp, an account administrator adds a chatbot to the project's Campfire and copies its lines URL, which starts with https://3.basecampapi.com/. Paste it below and choose what to post. Lines carry the title and a link, nothing private.

settings.integrations.kit.description: Send your newsletters from Kit. Readers who join a blog's mailing list are added to your Kit account with a tag for that blog. Readers who leave are taken off, and anyone who unsubscribes in Kit leaves the blog's list too. Each blog connects on its own.

Each blog connects on its own.

settings.externalKeys.description: Add your own API keys for external AI services. Keys are encrypted and stored securely, and used only for features you start. The assistant sends story context to that provider under that provider's data policy — Literary Universe cannot change those logs or caches.
settings.externalKeys.securityNote: Treat API keys like passwords. Never share them with anyone.
settings.externalKeys.delete.confirm: Remove the stored API key for this service? You can add it again later.

settings.ai.proofreadingWatchlist.title: Proofreading watchlist

settings.storyRecommendations.explained: Enable personalized story recommendations throughout the app based on your reading preferences and history.
settings.languages.readingLanguageExplai: When looking up stories we will offer you stories and their translations in this language unless you specify otherwise.
settings.languages.wordsPerMinuteExplain: We use this to estimate how long a story will take you to read. Leave it empty to use the average of {average, number} words per minute. Not sure about yours? Measure your reading speed.
settings.username.help: Your unique username on the platform
settings.interests.tags.custom.help: Enter comma separated list of tags
settings.interests.avoidGenres.help: Select genres you'd prefer not to see in recommendations.
settings.kindleEmail.explained: If you have this set, then where possible we will offer you the option to send stories to your Kindle with one click. You can find your Kindle email address in your Amazon settings under Content & Devices -> Devices -> select your Kindle to view its details and there you will find the email listed.
settings.tracking.title: Tracking & Statistics
settings.tracking.description: Track your reading and writing time to get detailed statistics on your reading habits and writing progress. You can view these statistics in your library and workshop.
settings.tracking.reading.title: Reading Time
settings.tracking.reading.description: Track time spent reading stories and chapters. This data helps you understand your reading habits and is shared anonymously with story authors to show them how engaged readers are with their work.
settings.tracking.writing.title: Writing Time
settings.tracking.writing.description: Track time spent writing stories, chapters, and encyclopedia entries. This includes detailed metrics like typing activity, word counts, and time-of-day patterns.
settings.apiKeys.create.title: Create New API Key
settings.interests.description: Tell us about your reading preferences to help us recommend content that matches your interests.
settings.interests.tags.help: Select up to 20 tags that interest you.
settings.recommendations.title: Story recommendations
settings.recommendations.mode: How should we recommend stories to you?
settings.recommendations.explained: Personalised uses your reading activity and favourite genres. Community shows what is popular with all readers, without profiling you. Chronological shows only the newest content and the stories you explicitly follow.
settings.externalKeys.sakanaHelp: To use your Fugu subscription, choose Subscription when creating your Sakana key and turn off pay-as-you-go fallback. Read <setup>Sakana's setup guide</setup> and check <terms>regional availability</terms> before connecting.
settings.externalKeys.googleHelp: Google AI Studio keys may let Google use prompts to improve products unless you use a paid Gemini API or Vertex project. Check <terms>Google's Gemini API terms</terms>. Literary Universe does not control Google's logs.

settings.tracking.socialButtons.title: Embedded social buttons
settings.tracking.socialButtons.descript: Choose whether social networks can load their like and share buttons in this browser. You can turn them off in cookie preferences. Regular sharing links remain available.
settings.ai.usage.title: Literary Universe AI usage
settings.ai.usage.off: AI on Literary Universe keys is switched off at the moment. The assistant still works with your own provider keys.
settings.ai.usage.explained: The assistant runs on Literary Universe keys by default and is paid from your usage balance. Each reply shows what it cost. Your own provider keys are an alternative and are never charged here.
settings.ai.usage.lasting: {amount} of what is left is credit, which does not reset.
settings.ai.usage.allowance: Your plan includes {amount} of AI usage each calendar month. Unused usage does not carry over.
settings.ai.usage.noMonthlyAllowance: Your plan has no monthly AI allowance. Storyteller includes one, or buy credits below.
settings.ai.credits.title: Credits
settings.ai.credits.explained: Credits are added to your balance and never expire. Your monthly allowance is used first. Prices are in US dollars before tax; checkout adds tax and can show your local currency.
settings.ai.credits.bought: Thank you. Your credits appear in your balance once Stripe confirms the payment, usually within a minute.
settings.ai.credits.failed: Checkout could not be started. Please try again later.
settings.ai.usage.summaryError: The usage summary could not be loaded.
settings.ai.usage.none: No platform AI usage yet this month.
settings.ai.usage.pricesExplained: USD per million tokens, including the platform margin. A cache write stores the start of the conversation once; later turns re-read it as cached input. Web search is charged per search, on top of the tokens its results add.
settings.ai.usage.priceDeepL: DeepL translation and rephrasing in the assistant: {price} per million characters sent.

settings.apps.quickstart.title: Build on Literary Universe
settings.apps.quickstart.signIn: To let people sign in with Literary Universe, create an app below and give its client ID to any OpenID Connect library. Ask for the scopes {scopes} to get the person's username, name and avatar in the ID token. Every app must use PKCE with S256.
settings.apps.quickstart.api: To work with stories, add permissions to the app and send its access token to the GraphQL API at {graphql}. The TypeScript SDK ({sdk}) and the lu command line tool handle this for you. AI assistants connect to {mcp}.
settings.apps.quickstart.discovery: OpenID Connect libraries find every endpoint at {discovery}. For a script only you run, an API key is simpler.
settings.apps.quickstart.submit: When the app is ready for others, submit it. After a review it appears in Integrations and its sign-in page says Literary Universe reviewed it.
settings.apps.intro: Apps you build can let readers and writers sign in with their Literary Universe account and, with their permission, work with their stories.
settings.apps.editReview: Saving changes sends the app back to review. Until then it is not listed.
